newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Ross to discuss U.S. peace ideas with PLO, Israel.
newsitem.headline: Ross to discuss U.S. peace ideas with PLO, Israel.

text.p: U.S. special envoy Dennis Ross will meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Gaza on Wednesday to discuss reviving PLO-Israel peace talks suspended for a month, a PLO official said on Tuesday.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said the time of Netanyahu's meeting with Ross had yet to be set. Israel Radio had said the U.S. envoy would meet Netanyahu on Wednesday.

"Dennis Ross will meet President Arafat in Gaza at 7:30 p.m. (1630 GMT) to discuss ways to salvage the peace process suspended by Israeli intransigence," Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, general secretary of the Palestinian presidency, told Reuters.

Abdel-Rahim said they would discuss U.S. "ideas" before the Clinton administration formulates an initiative to break the peace deadlock which began when Israel decided to build a Jewish settlement on a hill Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim.

"They will discuss ideas to resolve the crisis in PLO-Israeli talks which was a result of Israel's decision to build a settlement on Jabal Abu Ghneim in Jerusalem and Israel's rejection to adhere to the basis of the peace deals," he said.
Abdel-Rahim said Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Viktor Posuvalyuk would meet Arafat in Gaza on Thursday to try to help revive the peace negotiations.
Israel wants Arafat to make a greater effort to halt violence and "terrorism". Palestinians demand a halt to the settlement project which Israel calls Har Homa.

Chief negotiator Saeb Erekat said during talks between a senior Palestinian delegation and U.S. officials in Washington last week "we were informed by the U.S. that all American efforts to get Israel to freeze Jabal Abu Ghneim settlement building have failed."
"They only promised to send Ross to meet President Arafat to discuss with him ideas which could be part of an American initiative," he said.

Abdel-Rahim said the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) believed Washington wanted to speed up Israel-PLO final status talks which will determine the status of the West Bank, including Arab East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip.

"The U.S. intends to push for speedy final status talks and to press for implementation of interim issues such as further Israeli redeployments from the West Bank, building a Palestinian port and airport and safe passages," he told Reuters.
Another PLO official said Ross will try to press Israel to refrain from unilateral actions that prejudge the outcome of final status talks on issues such as settlements and Jerusalem.
"But we believe Ross will try to convince Arafat that Jabal Abu Ghneim settlement is de facto, and we have to resume talks from there," the PLO official, insisting on anonymity, said.
"Ross will also try to push Palestinians to restore security coordination with Israel," he said.

Palestinians halted security cooperation with their Israeli counterparts after Netanyahu limited contacts to the security sphere -- dropping political talks -- after a Moslem militant bombing in Tel Aviv that killed three Israelis in March.
